clue.text: Clouds over the nanny's bristles

definitions.meaning: in old weather lore, wispy high cirrus streaks are named after a goat's coat, alongside mares' tails
a nanny is a female goat, so her bristles are her coat

explanation.walkthrough: 'over' only joins the two definitions. Cirrus clouds were traditionally called goat's hair or mares' tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a folk name for cirrus streaks, and literally the coarse coat of a she-goat.

clue.text: Coax independent lecturer to make acid

indicators.note: to make here means the letters are worked into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries to persuade an independent lecturer into producing a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is the anagram signal: COAX plus I and L are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxalic acid is a poisonous organic acid found in rhubarb leaves.

clue.text: Did this girl get her kicks from the farmer?

definitions.text: Did this girl get her kicks from the farmer?

parts.words: Did this girl get her kicks from the farmer?
parts.note: one sense is a high-kicking chorus dancer from a famous troupe; the other is someone who tills land

explanation.surface: A girl enjoys the thrills a farmer gives her.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tiller Girls were a British dance troupe famed for precision high kicks; a farmer who tills the soil is also so called.
explanation.definitionFit: A cultivator of soil, and a member of a high-kicking British chorus line.

clue.text: Brazier made hot soil

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
soil means earth

explanation.definitionFit: Both are places where a fire burns: a brazier is a metal fire basket, a hearth the floor of a fireplace.

clue.text: Annual receipts and levy report

parts.note: receipts means money coming in, income
a levy is a tax
a return is an official report or statement

explanation.surface: A yearly statement setting out earnings and the tax owed on them.
explanation.definitionFit: The yearly form a taxpayer files declaring earnings so the levy owed can be assessed.

clue.text: Somehow at Corsica in the Caribbean

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters get there by some unexplained route, rearranged

explanation.surface: The Mediterranean island Corsica has somehow turned up in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American country whose eastern coast lies on that sea.

clue.text: Was dame olgri once leader of Israel?

indicators.note: was invites the reader to ask what these jumbled words once were, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether some dame was formerly Israel's prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'olgri' is no word, a sign that DAME OLGRI is a jumble to be rearranged into the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel's fourth prime minister, serving 1969 to 1974.

clue.text: Put the paper down

parts.note: reads like laying a newspaper aside, but means sending an edition to be printed

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a newspaper edition being sent to the printers.

clue.text: Take off alone

parts.note: reads like an aircraft taking to the air with one pilot, but means to strike out independently

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for acting by oneself, from a pilot's first unaccompanied flight.

clue.text: Trifling as I dance all around the place

indicators.note: around the place means scattered everywhere, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carefree person dances all over, idly trifling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around the place' tells you to rearrange I DANCE ALL. 'Trifling' is a noun here, idle amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is idle flirting or playing about, the noun sense of trifling.

clue.text: Workshop where the boss and I operate initially

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word operate

explanation.surface: A workshop where my boss and I run things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not the manager but an ornamental knob, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or craftsman's working room, a synonym.

clue.text: Condition for being able to do it when inside, perhaps

definitions.text: Condition for being able to do it when inside, perhaps

parts.words: Condition for being able to do it when inside, perhaps
parts.note: one reading is having the hours needed for a task; the other is a prisoner sentenced to a term in jail

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom both for being allowed enough hours and for receiving a jail sentence.

clue.text: Foremost Tory book

parts.note: foremost means first in importance, prime
a Tory is on the political right, abbreviated R

explanation.definitionFit: A primer is an elementary schoolbook teaching reading or a subject's basics.

clue.text: Prove that the slab is designed properly

indicators.note: designed properly means the letters are arranged afresh to a plan

explanation.surface: An engineer shows that a concrete slab was made to the right design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed properly' signals rearranging THE SLAB IS; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a fact is to demonstrate it beyond doubt, a synonym.

clue.text: As well as not being in view?

definitions.text: As well as not being in view?

parts.words: As well as not being in view?
parts.note: points to the proverb about what happens to something no longer seen: it is also forgotten

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for forgotten, from the proverb pairing absence from sight with absence from thought.

clue.text: "Finish, good lady; the bright - - , and we are for the dark" Shakespeare's Anthony and Cleopatra)

definitions.text: "Finish, good lady; the bright - - , and we are for the dark" Shakespeare's Anthony and Cleopatra)

parts.words: "Finish, good lady; the bright - - , and we are for the dark" Shakespeare's Anthony and Cleopatra)
parts.note: the missing words complete Iras's line to Cleopatra, spoken as night and death approach

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Iras speaks the line in Act 5 of the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing words say the daylight has ended, a picture of life drawing to a close.

clue.text: Cue to look over

parts.note: a note at the foot of a page prompting the reader to turn to the other side

explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation for please turn over, printed as a prompt to continue reading overleaf.

clue.text: Please eat anything starting with the vegetable

indicators.note: starting means only the opening letters of these words are used

explanation.surface: A parent coaxes a child to eat anything, starting with the greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes the first letters of Please, Eat, Anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round green seed eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Single type of eon

indicators.note: type of suggests a different version of the word eon, its letters rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Single means just the one, a synonym.

clue.text: The English make a meal of bratwurst mit pommes frites

definitions.text: The English make a meal of bratwurst mit pommes frites

parts.words: The English make a meal of bratwurst mit pommes frites
parts.note: asks for the English rendering of a German dish of fried pork links with fries

explanation.walkthrough: 'The English' means the English translation, and 'make a meal of' plays on the idiom for overdoing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Translation: bratwurst is a pork link, pommes frites are fries, a staple British plate.

clue.text: Cut down half the annexe

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Cut down half the annexe (3)': 'Cut down' defines AXE, but half of ANNEXE is ANN or EXE, never AXE; no honest halving or selection gives the letters.

clue.text: A feline in charge of small matter

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A cat put in charge of something trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small matter' is not a trifle but the tiniest unit of matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic means relating to atoms, the tiny particles of matter.

clue.text: Her songs?

parts.note: her could stand for a woman by name, making these songs belong to her; also festive hymns

explanation.definitionFit: Christmas hymns, and with an apostrophe, belonging to a woman so named.

clue.text: Some current alimony is due to be paid

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the current maintenance payment is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is at the end of 'current' and the start of 'alimony'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental is a sum owed periodically for the use of property, what falls due.

clue.text: A following federation get foot sore

parts.note: the letter that follows A in the alphabet is B
a federation is a union of states

explanation.surface: A league that follows on gets a painful foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A following' means what comes after A: B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunion is a painful swelling on the big toe joint, a sore on the foot.

clue.text: Exercise cautious anxiety

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Exercise cautious anxiety (2,7)': 'cautious' looks garbled (likely 'caution'), and no parse accounts for 'anxiety'; a search of the exact text found nothing.

clue.text: Greek character sees doctor in Russian car

indicators.note: in places the doctor's letters inside the name of the car

parts.note: Lada is a Russian make of car
MB is a medical degree, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A Greek man sees a medic while sitting in a Lada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sees' is only a link; the car is the Soviet-built Lada, and the doctor is a Bachelor of Medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Not in balance like those who don't take exercise

definitions.meaning: of a boat or aircraft, poorly balanced in its load

definitions.text: like those who don't take exercise

explanation.walkthrough: A trim is a vessel's balance in the water; being trim is also being fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term for an unbalanced vessel, and an idiom for being physically unfit.

clue.text: Voiced by child worker

parts.note: a son is a child
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Something said by a child labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetics term: a voiced sound is produced with the vocal cords vibrating.

clue.text: Injury trussed up like a wooden sandwich!

definitions.text: Injury trussed up like a wooden sandwich!

parts.words: Injury trussed up like a wooden sandwich!
parts.note: a broken limb bound between strips of wood looks like a filling between slices of bread

explanation.definitionFit: Describes a fractured limb held rigid by a wooden support strapped along it.
